title: Choose models and a budget for a product launch's images and short videos
scenario: A tea brand launches a new iced tea. You run the studio plan: which kinds of model do the jobs, what limits shape the work, what it will cost and what you can accept from the client. The studio shot the product photos itself. Use the exhibit. Prices were copied from Google's Gemini API pricing page on 2026-10-06 and change often.
exhibit:
BRIEF:
  Job 1  50 social images, 1:1, 1K. Needed in 8 days.
  Job 2  One vertical teaser: 9:16, 1080p, 16 seconds, with sound,
         made from the studio's own product photos.
  Job 2b  The same teaser at about 20 seconds for a web banner. 720p is fine.
  Job 3  Check 25 shop photos sent by field staff: is the logo visible and facing front?
         4 of the 25 are HEIC files from phones.
  Client note: "Use these 8 stock-site photos as style references.
         We have not bought the licence yet; we will buy it if we like the result."

TOOLS (input -> output, from vendor docs):
  Claude            text + image -> text. Cannot generate images.
  Nano Banana 2.1   text + reference images -> image (generate and edit), 1K / 2K / 4K
  Veo 3.1           text or images -> video with audio
                    4, 6 or 8 s; 1080p and 4k only at 8 s; 16:9 or 9:16;
                    extension: +7 s per step, 720p only

PRICES (Gemini API pricing page, checked 2026-10-06):
  Nano Banana 2.1 image output, 1K image = 1,120 tokens
    Standard: $30 per 1M tokens    Batch: $15 per 1M tokens
  Veo 3.1 Standard: $0.40 per second (1080p)
  Veo 3.1 Fast:     $0.12 per second (1080p)

TEAM NOTES (ours, from the last campaign):
  Images: about 2 tries for every image we keep.
  Video: about 3 tries for every clip we keep.

GOOGLE GENERATIVE AI PROHIBITED USE POLICY (line):
  "Violates the rights of others, including privacy and intellectual property rights"
GEMINI API IMAGE DOCS (line):
  "Make sure you have the necessary rights to any images you upload."
GEMINI BATCH API DOCS (line):
  "Batch jobs are designed to complete within a 24-hour turnaround time."

questions.prompt: Which set of model types does the studio need for jobs 1, 2 and 3?

options.text: One Claude model for all three jobs.
options.explanation: Claude reads images and writes text. Its vision docs say it cannot generate, produce, edit, manipulate or create images, so it cannot do jobs 1 or 2.

options.text: An image model for job 1, a video model with audio for job 2, and a vision model for job 3.
options.explanation: Right. Start from the output you need: an image, a video with sound, and a written yes/no check. A media project is usually a small chain of models.

options.text: An image model for all three jobs, because a video is only moving images and a photo check is only a picture.
options.explanation: The image model makes images, not video with sound, and not a written check of photos. Each output needs the model type that makes it.

options.text: A video model for all three jobs.
options.explanation: A video model makes video with audio. Job 3 needs a written yes/no report, which is text output from a model that reads images.

questions.prompt: Four of the 25 shop photos are HEIC files. The shortlist for the logo check is Claude or OpenAI. What do you do first?

options.text: Send them as they are. All vision models accept HEIC.
options.explanation: The Gemini API docs list HEIC as a supported type, but the Claude and OpenAI image docs do not. Check the vendor's list before sending.

options.text: Convert the 4 HEIC files to JPEG, which both vendors list.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs list JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP, and the OpenAI docs list PNG, JPEG, WEBP and non-animated GIF. Neither lists HEIC, so convert phone photos first.

options.text: Drop the 4 HEIC photos from the check.
options.explanation: You would lose real shop photos for a problem a file conversion fixes.

options.text: Shrink all 25 photos to thumbnails.
options.explanation: Tiny images make mistakes more likely: the Claude docs warn about very small images under 200 pixels. Thumbnails also do not fix the file type.

questions.prompt: Which plan makes the ~20-second 720p banner version with the fewest edits?

options.text: One 20-second request at 720p.
options.explanation: Clips are 4, 6 or 8 seconds. Longer videos come from extension or editing.

options.text: One 8-second 1080p clip, extended twice.
options.explanation: Extension works at 720p only.

options.text: One 8-second 720p clip, extended twice by 7 seconds (22 s), trimmed to 20.
options.explanation: Right. Extension adds 7 seconds per step and works at 720p, which the banner allows.

options.text: One 8-second 4k clip, extended twice, then scaled down to 720p and trimmed to 20 seconds.
options.explanation: Extension works at 720p only, and 4k costs more.

questions.prompt: Jobs 1 and 2 run on Batch for images and Veo 3.1 Fast for video. Job 2b is not in this budget. Using the team notes, which budget is right?

options.text: About $2.76.
options.explanation: You pay for every try, not only for the keepers. This number skips the tries.

options.text: About $20.88.
options.explanation: The plan uses Veo 3.1 Fast at $0.12 per second. Standard is $0.40 per second.

options.text: About $7.44.
options.explanation: Right. Images: 100 tries x 1,120 tokens x $15 / 1M = $1.68. Video: 2 kept clips x 3 tries x 8 s x $0.12 = $5.76. Total $7.44.

options.text: About $9.12.
options.explanation: The images are due in 8 days, so they can wait for Batch, which is half the Standard price. At Standard they would cost $3.36, not $1.68.

questions.prompt: The client wants to use 8 unlicensed stock photos as style references now. What do you do?

options.text: Upload them now. The client can buy the licence later if they like the result, and the studio can delete them.
options.explanation: The Gemini docs ask you to make sure you have the necessary rights to any images you upload. The rule applies at upload, not after the result is liked.

options.text: Wait until the licence is bought, or use images the studio owns, such as its own product photos.
options.explanation: Right. The exhibit says to make sure you have the rights to any image you upload. Unlicensed photos are not the studio's to upload, and the studio's own photos are.

options.text: Upload them. They are only references and are not part of the final ad.
options.explanation: The docs say to have the rights to any image you upload, not only to images in the final result. Google's policy also forbids content that violates intellectual property rights.

options.text: Upload only 3 of the 8, so the risk is smaller.
options.explanation: Rights apply to each image you upload. Fewer unlicensed images is still unlicensed use.
